Dear Voaters,

I am a student in college looking for another martial art to try out/practice/adopt. I'm a part time security guard in a bar. I have thought long and hard about what martial art to take and have gone through a few.

Martial Arts:

  1. Tae Kwon Do (WTF): 2.5 years
  2. Muay Thai: 3 months (intense once a day, shins could only take it because of Tae Kwon Do)
  3. Krav Maga: 1 year (had the best of the best as a teacher you could possibly get in Canada)

I've been looking into one that would compliment every area. I thought I found it with Krav Maga but sparring is stupidly dangerous and restricted. It doesn't allow you to actually practice the movements properly and we both know if there is no hard spar there is no actual muscle memory (at least that's how it works for me).

I need:

  1. Versatility (weapons if possible/distance/strike/small locks)
  2. Limited but some ground play (going on the ground in a fight is almost a sure way of getting stomped by his friends, seen it happen to good BJJ practitioners)
  3. I don't really mind foul play.

Martial art I'm interesting in:

1- Kajukenbo (I have an 8th dan black belt in my town, incredibly reputated to the bone, original dog brother, etc.) 2- Combat Sambo (heard about it, might be a sham tbh kind of like 80% of Krav Maga schools, need opinions) 3- Hapkido (Combination of Tae Kwon Do and Aikido as far as I understood?)

I'm seriously considering Kajukenbo because: - It's pure hard spar, almost no protection. I love that, if there is one thing - Versatility, I saw some locks, almost like MMA but includes some weapon - Trainer, the trainer is ULTRA reputated and is known pretty well in the martial arts world

Any other suggestions? Tips? Advice?
Suggest me a martial art & advice on one I'm considering taking
Jeet Kune Do. It's more of a philosophy or set of concepts that you can apply to your existing knowledge to make your application of it more effective.
I do not need a philosophy really. I need more of an art. Brutal and efficient, but I'll keep it in mind. Jeet Kune Do feels too random imo.

Kali A.K.A Eskrima, Arnis or FMA (Filipino Martial Arts) seems like a good addition. While most martial arts focus on using a closed fist, the empty-handed aspects of Kali involve primarily slapping which is much less likely to lead to hand injuries.

The Kali techniques have developed so that anything you do with empty hand will translate into the weapons techniques that are taught as well, so you are learning the basis for empty-handed and weapons techniques at the same time. The Kali weapon techniques can also be applied with knives, sticks, or just about any rigid weapon as long as it's not much longer than your arm.

I have seen people compare Kali to Krav Maga. I do not have the personal experience to support this, but I understand that Kali is similar to Krav Maga in many ways, but with a much greater degree of depth. Kali is the military martial technique used throughout the Phillipines, and as such it is designed to do well on uneven or unreliable footing compared to many other martial arts. Its movements are quick and compact to minimize openings.

Combat sambo meets all of your criteria. Kali is the shit too. Ground game is great one on one but for multiple attackers it kinda sucks unless you pull guard and eye gouge as fast as possible than get back on or feet.
